subject: Dedicated capacity: timebox windows, credit pool & autoscale proposal (Pegasus AI)
messages:

Subject: Re: Capacity planning inputs (Q4 ramp)

Thanks Lauren — attaching the traffic forecast and our go-to-market ramp plan. Key points: weekly batch jobs for embeddings kicking off Nov 15, expected peak API TPS around Black Friday (Nov 26) with an unpredictable spike window between 1–3 hours, and a sustained 2x baseline for the first 2 business weeks after launch.

We also flagged procurement to start the paperwork; they asked for a clear definition of "burst window" and how charges are applied when you do dedicated plus transient burst. Samir (CloudZone) is CC'd because they're our infra partner and will want to know prewarm expectations.

Attachments: pegasus_traffic_forecast_q4.xlsx, pegasus-MAP-v1.pdf

Subject: Re: Capacity planning inputs (Q4 ramp)

Hi Ava — got the files, thanks. High level response inlined below and Monica/Karthik/Rishi are on the thread to scope the dedicated+burst guardrails.

Quick answers up front:
- "Burst window" for our Dedicated offering is a configurable timebox (we typically recommend <= 6 hours per day in your contract during predictable peaks; shorter windows can be negotiated).
- Billing: base Dedicated commit covers reserved GPU slabs; burst consumption above committed throughput will draw from a transient credit pool and be billed at a higher per-token/VM rate unless we convert to a temporary reserve (we can discuss conversion triggers).

Ava — can you confirm the expected weekly cadence of the spike (days of week/hours) and whether the embedding batch can be shifted off-peak? If Black Friday spike is highly unpredictable, we should discuss a pre-authorized temporary reserve or a rapid uplift window with a pre-signed SLA addendum to avoid throttling.

I asked Monica to propose concrete timebox templates and Karthik to draft the minimal contract language for the transient credit pool. Rishi — can you prep a short options sheet (cost delta vs. risk of throttling) for procurement?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@pegasus.ai>

Date: 2026-10-26T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning inputs (Q4 ramp)

Hi all — dug into the forecast. A few proposals from SRE/solutions side:

1) Timebox model (recommended):
   - Daily burst window: up to 4 hours/day between 00:00–06:00 PT or 18:00–23:00 PT (you pick), 21-day rolling cap of 60 hours/month.
   - Emergency uplift: 2x burst for up to 2 occurrences/month (requires a 15-minute on-call acknowledgement).

2) Credit pool:
   - We allocate a transient credit pool equal to 10% of committed capacity by default; unused credits expire monthly.
   - Option to pre-purchase additional credits at 70% of on-demand uplift rate (saves ~18% vs. pay-as-you-go uplift).

3) Prewarm lanes:
   - For Black Friday we can prewarm a lightweight cache & KV-prefix to speed cold-starts. Prewarm takes ~18 minutes per slab; we can schedule prewarm jobs with CloudZone.

4) Autoscale policy (runtime settings):
   - Scale trigger: sustained 95th-percentile token throughput > 1.8x baseline for 90s.
   - Max transient multiplier: 3x committed slab (hard cap).
   - Eviction policy: oldest preemptible jobs are reclaimed first; priority jobs (embedding batches) marked with a reserve tag keep a minimal slab during eviction.

Attachments: draft autoscale runbook stub (will upload to Drive).

Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@pegasus.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Samir Khatri <samir@cloudzone.com>
Date: 2026-10-27T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning inputs (Q4 ramp)

Following Monica's notes — adding the minimal contract language snippet we recommend for the "transient credit pool" and timebox enforcement so procurement has clarity:

- Transient credit definition: credits represent compute-time beyond committed slab measured in GPU-minutes; credits are consumed in chronological order and drawn before on-demand billing.
- Timebox enforcement: customer can define up to two daily burst windows in the contract; requests outside these windows will be queued and can be auto-accepted if credits are available.
- Billing fallback: if credits exhausted, we will attempt a 10-minute rapid uplift to on-demand at pre-agreed rate; if uplift fails due to capacity, Redwood will throttle requests back to committed throughput and issue a capacity incident.

Also — propose an SLA addendum for Black Friday temporary reserve: a 48-hour pre-authorized uplift with a minimum 72-hour notice to Redwood's ops team for provisioning a pre-warmed reserve slab. This gives Pegasus deterministic capacity and removes throttling risk for the critical window.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: procurement@pegasus.ai, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning inputs (Q4 ramp)

Procurement team — quick cost/options note to help you choose:

Option A — Baseline Dedicated + small transient pool
  - Commit: 40 GPU-slabs (baseline)
  - Transient credits: 4 GPU-slabs equivalent/month (10%)
  - Estimated uplift cost (if fully used): +28% vs committed monthly spend

Option B — Baseline + pre-authorized temporary reserve for Black Friday
  - Commit: 40 GPU-slabs
  - Black Friday reserve: +30 slabs for 48 hours (pre-warmed)
  - Estimated uplift cost: discrete surcharge for the 48-hour reserve (~+12% of monthly spend) but near-zero throttling risk

Option C — Pre-purchase extra credits at discounted uplift rate
  - Commit: 40 GPU-slabs
  - Buy extra credits (20 slabs/month) at 70% of uplift rate — saves ~15–20% if you expect frequent spikes

Tradeoffs: A is cheapest up-front; B gives deterministic availability for the critical weekend; C is middle-ground for repeated moderate spikes.

I can convert these into line-item pricing for your finance team if you share the vendor billing contact.

— Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Ava Reynolds <ava.reynolds@pegasus.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@pegasus.ai, Samir Khatri <samir@cloudzone.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning inputs (Q4 ramp)

Team — this is great, thanks for the clarity. Procurement prefers Option B for Black Friday (deterministic reserve) and Option C for ongoing monthly protection. Two asks before we finalize:

1) Can Redwood provide an operational playbook (1–2 pages) we can attach to the SLA addendum that documents the 15-minute on-call acknowledgement, uplift sequence, and post-event reconciliation (credits used + conversion to reserve)?
2) Samir — can CloudZone confirm prewarm orchestration (we need a runbook showing the 18-minute per-slab prewarm timing and the API hook you'll call to trigger it)?

If you can drop the SLA draft and the 1–2 page playbook into the Drive link, procurement will start drafting redlines. We aim to sign before Nov 10 to meet provisioning lead times.

Attaching: sla-draft-pegasus.docx (initial language)

— Ava
